title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models

Title:DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:Online reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tunes diffusion models with black-box rewards, but reverse-process methods such as Flow-GRPO are limited in efficiency by poor credit assignment, while forward-process methods such as DiffusionNFT are efficient yet unstable without carefully tuned exponential-moving-average (EMA) off-policy training. We show that NFT-style objectives contain a hidden forward--reverse consistency force that joint positive--negative training cancels only partially, and that EMA stabilizes training through restoration rather than off-policy rollouts. We introduce DiffusionART (Diffusion Reinforcement with Aggregation-First Reward Tilting), which aggregates each prompt's rewards into a shared reward-improving direction for reverse-process states, removing the consistency force by construction, and adds a trust-region-masked second update for drift-adaptive restoration without EMA tuning. It requires no differentiable reward model, remains effective with fewer samples per prompt, and supports pairwise reward models (DiffusionART-Pairwise). Across image and video generation, DiffusionART trains efficiently and stably without per-task tuning. In particular, on HunyuanVideo-13B with equally weighted visual and motion quality rewards, DiffusionART reaches the late-stage mean reward levels of DiffusionNFT and Flow-GRPO-Fast with 12.02 and 11.72 times fewer GPU hours, respectively, while achieving 28.8% and 53.0% higher mean training rewards.

report.summary: DiffusionART is a new reinforcement-learning method that fine-tunes diffusion models efficiently and stably without EMA tuning, cutting GPU hours dramatically on image and video generation.
report.background: Online reinforcement learning is increasingly used to align diffusion models with human or automated preferences, especially for image and video generation. Existing methods face a trade-off: reverse-process approaches like Flow-GRPO are stable but inefficient due to poor credit assignment, while forward-process approaches like DiffusionNFT are efficient but unstable without carefully tuned exponential-moving-average off-policy training. The paper argues that DiffusionNFT-style objectives contain a hidden forward-reverse consistency force, and that EMA mainly stabilizes training through restoration rather than off-policy rollout correction. DiffusionART builds on this analysis to deliver stable, scalable RL fine-tuning without per-task EMA tuning, differentiable reward models, or large sample budgets.
key_points: DiffusionART targets the efficiency-stability trade-off in online RL for diffusion models. Reverse-process methods such as Flow-GRPO suffer from poor credit assignment, while forward-process methods like DiffusionNFT are efficient but unstable without EMA tuning. The paper identifies and removes a hidden forward-reverse consistency force that prior joint positive-negative training only partially cancels.

The core technique is aggregation-first reward tilting. It aggregates each prompt's rewards into a shared reward-improving direction for reverse-process states, eliminating the consistency force by construction. This allows effective training with fewer samples per prompt and does not require a differentiable reward model, broadening compatibility with black-box and pairwise reward models.

A trust-region-masked second update provides drift-adaptive restoration, replacing EMA-based stabilization. This makes training stable without per-task EMA hyperparameter tuning. The method also supports DiffusionART-Pairwise for pairwise reward models, extending its applicability beyond scalar reward signals.

Across image and video generation, DiffusionART trains efficiently and stably without per-task tuning. On HunyuanVideo-13B with equally weighted visual and motion quality rewards, it reaches the late-stage mean reward levels of DiffusionNFT and Flow-GRPO-Fast using 12.02 and 11.72 times fewer GPU hours, respectively, while achieving 28.8% and 53.0% higher mean training rewards.

The results suggest that careful reward aggregation and trust-region updates can make online RL for diffusion models practical at scale. The method's sample efficiency and lack of EMA tuning reduce engineering overhead, potentially making preference alignment and reward-based fine-tuning more accessible for large image and video generation models.
report.impact: DiffusionART could significantly lower the cost and complexity of aligning diffusion models with human or automated preferences. For the AI industry, it offers a path to cheaper, more scalable RL fine-tuning of large image and video models, reducing GPU-hour requirements and manual hyperparameter tuning. For developers, it simplifies reward-based training by removing EMA tuning and differentiable reward model dependencies, while supporting black-box and pairwise rewards. For regular users, the practical benefit is faster iteration and better-aligned generative models, especially in video generation where quality and motion coherence remain challenging. If replicated and open-sourced, it may become a standard component in diffusion post-training pipelines.
report.tools: Readers can follow Flow-GRPO and DiffusionNFT for baseline comparisons, HunyuanVideo for large-scale video generation, and Hugging Face Diffusers for diffusion model fine-tuning. TRL, DeepSpeed or FSDP, and Weights & Biases are useful for RL training loops, distributed scaling, and experiment tracking. Watch for an official DiffusionART code release on arXiv or GitHub, and test it against existing reward models such as ImageReward, HPSv2, and VideoScore.
